text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Lands and Valuation Minister Peter Fachi has threatened to sue opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) vice president Gwanda Chakuamba for defamation after a newspaper story alleged he took money from chiefs to pay solicitors who would help them secure land.

- Mozambique Minister of Transport Paul Muxanga is expected to hold talks with his Malawian counterpart Harry Thompson to update him and the Malawi business community on the progress of rehabilitating the Nacala railway line and the Nacala port.
- Civil Servants Trade Union leader Thomas Banda and his family were attacked and robbed over the weekend in a Blantyre township by armed bandits, family sources said.

- Eleven people died of suffocation and burns caused by charcoal heaters and fires since winter started. Several others have lost property like houses, tobacco, clothes and maize stores, police said in a press statement.
- The ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) and opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) supporters were reported celebrating victory before results of by-elections in six constituencies were announced.
